findings.evidence: “Generate candidates using distinct patterns: compounds ... prefix/suffix ... evocative real words, coined blends, and carefully justified abbreviations.” Much of Procedure and Output activates familiar naming practices; the strongest additional knowledge is concentrated in the registration, renewal, homograph, and HSTS gotchas.
findings.fix: Compress the common naming-pattern recipe and routine output guidance. Preserve the less-obvious multilingual, registration-status, renewal-cost, and deployment constraints.

findings.evidence: “Rank, don't overclaim” asks for rationale and trade-offs but gives no decision order when pronunciation, distinctiveness, TLD preference, and budget conflict.
findings.fix: Apply hard language, confusion, and budget constraints before ranking. Then rank surviving candidates using the user's stated priorities, explicitly explaining any trade-off between memorability, descriptiveness, spelling reliability, and recurring cost.

findings.evidence: “Provides exactly or at least 12 candidate names” accepts more than the 12 names requested by the prompt.
findings.fix: Require exactly 12 distinct candidates in this test and separately verify the requested grouping and top-three explanations.

findings.evidence: “If no live lookup is performed, label every candidate unverified.” The live-lookup branch does not explicitly resolve timeouts, rate limits, unsupported TLDs, or ambiguous responses into an output status.
findings.fix: Define failed or inconclusive lookups as unknown/unverified, never available. Explain when to retry through a registrar, and distinguish an authoritative registration result from confirmed purchase availability.
